sections.heading: Title
sections.text: VectorMapNet is the first end-to-end pipeline that reads onboard camera and LiDAR and predicts a sparse set of polylines — the primitive planners actually use. It skips rasterization entirely and sets a new state of the art.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Self-driving cars need HD maps marking lanes, boundaries, and crosswalks. Today these are annotated by hand, which is costly and does not scale. Learning methods instead predict a dense pixel grid, but it carries no individual elements and needs brittle post-processing.

sections.heading: Motivation
sections.text: The authors argue mapping should happen online, from the car's own sensors, and the model should output the final representation directly. Prior methods rasterize then vectorize with a hand-designed step; VectorMapNet removes that detour and predicts geometry end to end.

sections.heading: Contribution
sections.text: VectorMapNet makes three contributions. It predicts vectorized outputs directly from sensors, with no rasterization or post-processing. It uses the polyline as one flexible primitive whose vertex order encodes direction. And it adapts detection transformers to locate elements in bird's-eye view.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: VectorMapNet has three stages. A bird's-eye-view extractor maps each modality into a shared space: cameras through a ResNet and IPM, LiDAR through PointPillars, fused by concatenation. A detection transformer with element queries locates each element as keypoints. An autoregressive polyline generator then emits ordered vertices, trained with detection and generation losses.

sections.heading: Dataset / Benchmark
sections.text: VectorMapNet is evaluated on nuScenes and Argoverse2. Following HDMapNet, predicted polylines are compared to ground truth for crosswalks, lane dividers, and road boundaries. It reports Chamfer-distance AP and a new Fréchet-distance AP that respects vertex order, plus 3D evaluation.

sections.heading: Key Result
sections.text: VectorMapNet sets a new state of the art. It beats HDMapNet by 14.2 mAP on nuScenes and 14.6 on Argoverse2. Gains hold across sensors: nearly eighteen points camera, ten LiDAR, over fourteen fusion. Two-stage fine-tuning pushes fusion to 53.7 mAP versus 31.0.

sections.heading: Ablation Study
sections.text: Two ablations stand out. Representing each element by a bounding box with two keypoints beats the alternatives by two Fréchet and over seven Chamfer points. Two-stage training, teacher forcing then fine-tuning on predicted keypoints, adds about seven mAP for camera and eight for fusion.

sections.heading: Headline Numbers
sections.text: To summarize: VectorMapNet exceeds the previous state of the art by 14.2 mAP on nuScenes and 14.6 on Argoverse2. Its best configuration, fusion with fine-tuning, reaches 53.7 mAP where HDMapNet reaches 31. Gains span sensors: about eighteen for camera, ten for LiDAR, fourteen for fusion.

sections.heading: Takeaway
sections.text: The takeaway: HD mapping needs no rasterize-then-vectorize detour. Treating mapping as detection plus autoregressive polyline generation, VectorMapNet produces directional vector maps from sensors, beats rasterized pipelines by double digits, and extends to centerlines.
